newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco Chuquicamata supervisors in pay talks.
newsitem.headline: Codelco Chuquicamata supervisors in pay talks.

text.p: Unions representing around 700 supervisors at Chilean state copper company Codelco's huge Chuquicamata mine are in talks to renew a pay deal which expires at the end of the month, said a union official.
"We are in talks. The company's reply to our demands should reach the unions' hands by May 23," said the official, who declined to be named.
The supervisors will vote on May 27 whether to accept the offer or go on strike in early June, he said.
The supervisors are demanding a change in pay scales as well as health and education benefits.
Any walkout by the supervisors, who co-ordinate miners' daily work, would paralyze the pit which produces over 600,000 tonnes of fine copper a year, said the union official.
But a Chuquicamata official said the impact of any strike was not clear.
"They have a relevant role but it is difficult to guess what the impact of a strike would be," he said.

Over 7,000 miners at the pit walked out last year, halting production for 10 days in May. The strike marked the start of a wave of discontent in Chile's all-important copper industry which has suffered a rash of strikes in recent months.
